newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland's TSB cuts mortgage rates by up to 0.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's TSB cuts mortgage rates by up to 0.5 pct.

text.p: TSB Bank said on Friday that it was cutting mortgage interest rates by up to 0.5 percent with effect from the start of business on April 8.
The move will see TSB's discounted variable mortgage rate, for those borrowing 80 percent or more of the house value, fall to 5.5 percent from 5.9 percent.
New borrowers to TSB Bank who opt for a fixed rate mortgage until the year 2000 will get a rate of 6.9 percent, down from 7.4 percent previously, the bank said in a statement.

"Today's interest rate adjustment is further evidence of TSB Bank's commitment to ensure that our customers benefit, as much as possible, from the current financial climate," TSB's general manager of advances, Tony O'Connell, said.
"We are particularly pleased to provide extra benefits to first-time buyers who are experiencing increasing difficulties as house prices continue to rise," he said.
